sentences.text: 3. A s
per the prosecution story

, minor prosecutrix submitted an application in writing before police alleging that on 28.10.2021 at around 07:00 pm, Rajesh took her towards agricultural field and committed rape upon her and threatened to eliminate her, if she discloses the incident to anyone.
Thereafter, on several occasions, he raped her.
Thereafter, Rajesh started to bring other persons at home , he by taking money from those persons, was making her available to them for rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault by those persons.
In Navratri time, Rajesh called one truck driver and handed-over her to him and he too committed rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.
F.I.R. was registered.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is in jail for last one year and two months.
She has not committed any office.
She is innocent.
She has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
She has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution story.
The main allegations are against Rajesh Sanodiya.
The trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail pending the trial.
5 . O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.
6 . In this case the main allegations are against Rajesh Sanodiya.
Prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial court.
She has not supported the prosecution story in toto.
As per the status report received from the trial court out of 21 witnesses only six witnesses have been examined so far.
Final conclusion of the trial will take considerable time.

Therefore, having taken into consideration change in circumstances,material on record including custody period, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant - Krishna Bai be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

She shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8 . This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Krishna Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34768452/
